addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` gives a concrete rule: an action that must happen, the conditions that trigger it, and any limit or default. Does `item.text` state that rule's action together with its limit or default, in its own words or the statement's, as something the item will do? A mention of the topic, a promise to 'handle' it gracefully, or a goal without the concrete action does not count. Judge whether the rule's content is present only, not whether anything else in the item conflicts with it.

criteria.yes: The item states the anchor's required action and its limit or default as part of the plan.
criteria.no: The item is silent on the rule, names only its topic or a vague intent, or plans a different action than the one the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: The item states some of the rule's concrete content, but it cannot be told whether the required action itself is planned.

contradicted.instructions: List to yourself the concrete commitments `item.text` makes. Does any of them rule out what `anchor.statement` requires, or require something the statement rules out, for a case the statement governs? Omission is not conflict, and commitments about cases outside the statement are not conflicts. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: At least one concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires for a case it governs.
criteria.no: No concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: A commitment in the item might rule out the requirement, but it is too ambiguous to tell.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor (`anchor.statement`, `anchor.scope`). Would someone checking that the plan honours `anchor.statement` need to read this item, because the item builds, changes, or relies on the behaviour, component, or queue the anchor is about, as listed in `anchor.scope`? Judge subject overlap only, not compliance.

criteria.yes: The item builds, changes, or relies on something named in anchor.statement or anchor.scope, so a reviewer of this anchor must read it, even if the item ignores or breaks the anchor.
criteria.no: The item is about an unrelated part of the system; a reviewer of this anchor could skip it.
criteria.unclear: The item text does not say enough to tell what part of the system it touches.

acceptance_table.rationale: Approved pass fixture of the locked anchor: resend of a busy response up to a configurable max_sends with default 5.
Approved fail fixture: never resending a 429 is irreconcilable with the statement's must-resend rule; it does not carry the directive.
States every element of the statement: the three statuses, resend, configurable maximum number of sends, default 5.
Changes the send path and the runner queue (named in scope) but says nothing about busy responses or resend; silence is not conflict.
Names the topic (busy responses) but carries none of the directive's specific content: no resend, no maximum number of sends, no default; a vague intent neither carries nor breaks the rule.
The statement requires 502 and 529 responses to be resent by the layer; never resending them cannot be reconciled with it and the directive is absent.
A type definition unrelated to busy-response handling, resend, holdoff or the runner queue.
Boundary of the limit: stopping after the fifth send at the default is exactly 'until a configurable maximum number of sends, 5 by default, is reached'.
The statement only governs 429, 502 and 529; not resending other statuses is outside it and does not conflict, while the busy rule is carried.

data.explanation: 28 role-complete bundles (baseline included) x 9 frozen oracle cases x 2 repeats: 504 calls, 0 retries. Bundle b-r2-a1-c3 is the top-ranked semantically accepted set: 54/54 role cells, 18/18 threshold-0 verdicts, 9/9 stable cases, zero regressions against the baseline. Confidence is diagnostic only; production review keeps the 0.6 threshold. Anchor-tuning rationale: the baseline (current questions) was rejected on topical-1 only: a generic 'handle busy responses gracefully' item drew addressed=unclear instead of no (verdict underspecified instead of not_addressed), because the current addressed criteria route topic-only allusions to unclear. The sealed addressed question (add-concrete-action) requires the rule's concrete action with its limit or default and classifies topic-only mentions as no, which matches the authority: a vague intent does not carry the directive. 18 of 28 bundles were semantically accepted; selection, scores and rankings are the runner's. Runner note: the auto-generated cross-product bundle IDs contain '+', which the runner's own safe-id check rejects (TOURNAMENT.CANDIDATES_INVALID); the same 27-bundle cross product was supplied as explicit bundles with safe IDs as the candidates schema permits.
